private_tutoring.claim_85pct_verification: VERIFIED AS TRACED, WITH CAVEAT: 'about 85% of senior secondary students' appears in Bray & Lykins (2012) 'Shadow Education: Private Supplementary Tutoring and Its Implications for Policy Makers in Asia' (ADB/CERC), Executive Summary, uncited; Box 1 attributes the figure to Caritas (2010): 85.5% senior secondary (81.9% middle, 72.5% lower), n=898 secondary students. It is a 2010 NGO survey figure, not a census; Bray et al 2014 (2011/12) measured 71.8% for S6 (past 12 months) and Bray & Kwok found 70.3% for S6-7 in 1998/99. So 85% is the high end; 70-85% range for senior secondary is defensible.

outbound_mobility.note_computation: share_of_bachelors_outside_pct = outside_bachelors / bachelors_all, my arithmetic from EDB tables; 2013,2014,2016,2017,2018,2021 not retrieved (SCMP: 2021 14.3% of full-time students outside HK; 2020 peak 14.5%).
outbound_mobility.trend: Outside-HK share of S6 leavers' full-time study peaked at 14.5% (2020), fell to 6.5% (2025); absolute outside count peaked ~6,009 (2020), 2,671 in 2025. Mainland's share of those going out rose from ~22% (2012) / 17% (2015) to 47% (2025); Taiwan fell from 31% (2015) to 7% (2025).
outbound_mobility.assessment_of_half_claim: NOT SUPPORTED by EDB data for S6 school leavers. Even in the 2020 peak, 25.6% of S6 leavers' bachelor's places were outside HK and 14.5% of all full-time students; in 2024-25 it is 13-14% of bachelor's places and 6.5-7.8% of full-time students. Caveats: (1) EDB survey undercounts leavers who went abroad and did not respond; (2) it excludes non-S6 routes (IB/international school students, who skew abroad) and repeaters later going abroad; (3) 'about half' might be true for IB/international-school pupils or for elite/high-scoring pupils, or might refer to Mainland-origin/other subgroup - not tested. Could also be a mix-up with 1980s-90s emigration/overseas study when the local degree supply was ~2-3% then ~18% of cohort (not verified).
